meta.title: Ondalux Heatmap — WiFi heat maps, designed and measured
meta.description: Free, open-source desktop app to design WiFi networks on your floor plans: predictive heat maps, AP catalog, on-site surveys and professional PDF reports.

hero.title:
WiFi heat maps,
designed and measured.
hero.lead: Plan WiFi networks on your floor plans: predict coverage, place the right access points, survey on site and deliver professional reports — all in one fast desktop app.
hero.alt: Ondalux Heatmap showing a signal heat map over an office floor plan with four access points

features.title: Everything you need to design great WiFi
features.lead: From the first floor plan to the final report, without switching tools.

items.title: Predictive design
items.text: Draw walls with real materials — drywall, concrete, glass, doors — and watch the coverage update instantly as you move access points.

items.title: AP catalog
items.text: 119 models from 15 vendors with radio values taken from official datasheets. Or enter your own access point data by hand.

items.title: Ceiling or wall mounting
items.text: Ceiling APs radiate all around; wall APs use a directional pattern you can aim right on the plan.

items.title: Automatic wall detection
items.text: Import a plan and get walls proposed from the PDF's vector lines or from the image — straight, diagonal and curved. Review, pick materials, done.

items.title: On-site survey
items.text: Walk the site and record real WiFi scans with your laptop. See the measured heat map, interpolated with IDW or kriging.

items.title: Predicted vs. measured
items.text: A difference map and statistics show where reality beats or misses the prediction, so you can calibrate the model.

items.title: Six heat maps
items.text: Signal strength, SNR, SINR, number of APs heard, channel overlap and requirements met — for every band.

items.title: Professional reports
items.text: A modern PDF with the AP placement, every heat map, coverage gaps and recommendations. Plus PNG and CSV exports.

items.title: 3D view
items.text: See the plan in 3D with walls at their real height and thickness over the heat map. Orbit, pan and zoom.

items.title: Multi-floor buildings
items.text: One plan per floor — or every page of a PDF — with slab loss. APs on nearby floors add their signal.

items.title: Always up to date
items.text: The app tells you when a new version is out, with what's new. You decide when to install it.

items.title: Portable and private
items.text: One file, no installer, no account. It works offline and your floor plans never leave your computer.

how.title: From floor plan to report in six steps
how.lead: A guided workflow that keeps the next step in sight.

steps.title: Import the floor plan
steps.text: PNG, JPG or PDF. Vector PDFs exported from CAD give the best results.

steps.title: Calibrate the scale
steps.text: Click two points of a known distance — a door, a dimension line — and type it.

steps.title: Draw or detect walls
steps.text: Pick a material for each wall, or let the beta wall detection propose them for you.

steps.title: Place access points
steps.text: Choose a model from the catalog, set channels and power, and check coverage live.

steps.title: Survey on site
steps.text: Optional: record real scans and compare them with the prediction.

steps.title: Export the report
steps.text: A PDF in English or Spanish, ready to send to your client.

download.title: Download Ondalux Heatmap
download.lead: Free and open source. A single portable file: download it and run it — no installer, no account.
download.smartscreen: The app is not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may show a warning the first time. Click “More info” and then “Run anyway”.
download.other: macOS and Linux versions are in development.

items.a: Yes. Ondalux Heatmap is open source under the MIT or Apache-2.0 license, with no subscriptions, accounts or limits.

items.q: Do I need to install anything?
items.a: No. It is a single portable .exe: download it, double-click it and start working. You can run it from a USB drive.

items.q: Which floor plans can I import?
items.a: PNG, JPG and PDF. A PDF with several pages becomes one floor per page. Vector PDFs exported from CAD work best, especially for automatic wall detection.

It uses a path loss model plus the loss of every wall crossed (2D per floor, with the loss of the slabs between floors), without reflections. It is a design estimate: survey the site to confirm and calibrate it.
Yes, on Windows with the computer's built-in WiFi adapter. Scanning on macOS and Linux is still in development.

items.q: Are my floor plans uploaded anywhere?
items.a: No. Everything stays on your computer: there is no account, no cloud and no telemetry. It only checks once a day whether a new version is out (you can turn that off).
The app and the reports are available in English and Spanish.
Write to support@ondaluxheatmap.com with your question; attaching the .lux project or the floor plan helps a lot.
